chunk_map.heading: H1/lede: Prep the run, fill the gaps
Phase 1: Pick the task you'll send off
Push back until the task is one end-to-end slice
Phase 2: Build the ranked list of what will hurt the agent
Correct the list and reprioritise it
Fill the worst two or three gaps
Match each fill to its shape and home
Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase
Compare notes, then tidy the folder

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
Live-demo beats survive a text read.
Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: chunk 6 carries four bold handles (fill-shape menu names) — over the ≤1-per-slide default, but this is the maintainer-attested named-handle menu from the 2026-07-09 emphasis pass, not the pre-pass bolded-lead-sentence monoculture the rule targets; harm (visual noise drowning the real handle) is absent since each bold span is a coined checklist-item name, not a whole sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/walk-and-send-off.md --report: heaviest slide 'Match each fill to its shape and home' 189 words / 4 bullets vs 210-word cap; oversized: 0 across all 8 slides. Confirms the previously-recorded figures, no drift since the last PASS.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: No fix needed; flagging that 189/210 is the tightest margin in the file and the slide most likely to break on any future addition to the four fill-shape bullets.
